relationships.subject: AM-2099
relationships.evidence_quote: On average, 600 nM AM-2099 inhibited 73 ± 13% of the sodium current remaining in 10 nM or 30 nM suzetrigine

relationships.subject: Nav1.7
relationships.object: human DRG neuron action potential threshold
relationships.evidence_quote: AM-2099 almost always (37 of 38 neurons) produced a depolarizing shift in the action potential threshold, determined by short (0.5 ms) current injections of increasing magnitude (Figure 4).

relationships.subject: Nav1.8
relationships.evidence_quote: A major difference is that inhibiting Nav1.8 channels was generally much more effective than Nav1.7 inhibition in reducing repetitive firing during 1 s current injections (Figure 7D).

key_findings: Selective Nav1.7 inhibition (AM-2099) in human DRG neurons at 37C shifts action potential threshold depolarized, raises rheobase and refractory period, and lowers upstroke velocity, but little affects repetitive firing.
Nav1.8 inhibition reduces repetitive firing much more than Nav1.7 inhibition, possibly explaining clinical efficacy differences.
